description: The 5-row template as a template page opens it: every image-set item unranked (two in a subfolder), no title, default layout. Every tier id sits at its template position, so no row writes its id.
7-row Overwatch ranking with an empty D tier and a title with curly quotes, an apostrophe, a ZWJ family emoji, a flag, CJK, Hangul, Arabic and a backslash.

A 5-row list whose rows were dragged into a new order (the tier ids moved with the items, the labels stayed) and then renamed: emoji, double quotes, an empty label, Arabic, HTML-like text. Only the rows whose id left its template position write it.
A 3-row list with no items and no title.
The custom row template (no tp): every row writes its id, also ids that match a template, and ids that no template has.

Every item kind: image-set ids (nested filenames, several sets), link images (trusted and other hosts, a query string and fragment, a Unicode host, percent-encoding, one without a label) and device images (legacy-style and UUID-style local ids, one without a label). Labels with quotes, a backslash, a ZWJ emoji and a flag.
Tier labels on the right and item labels hidden.
Tier labels on top, item labels shown, 7 rows.
Tier labels on the left (the default, left out) and item labels hidden, 3 rows.
A title made of spaces (kept, because it is not empty), tier labels that keep spaces, a line break and a tab, an emptied label, and empty rows.
The 5-row template with one row added (a manual tier): the added row and every row below the template's last position write their id.
The same image-set item twice and the same link image twice (with different labels): the decoder keeps duplicates; removing them is the app's job.
Every item of all seven packages at bf2ff6e (430 items) spread over the 7-row template: the same list as generated.json v2-all-items-every-package, for link length comparisons.
A typical list: 20 Overwatch heroes in the 5-row template with a short title, most of them ranked. Used for link length comparisons.

Long strings: v3 has no cap on string lengths (A43). A title of 2,000 UTF-16 code units (1,000 emoji), a tier name, tier id, item id and labels of 1,000, a device image id of 64 (the most the device id rule allows), and a link image address of 4,000 characters.
100 rows (the cap), custom template, one item in every tenth row.
5,000 items (the cap) over the 7-row template: short item ids (the item count is what this entry checks), every tenth item a device image.

Ids that name no image-set item keep their stored label as {i, c} (A45): an id with a dot from an image set the app does not have, an id the image sets never had, and a label with quotes and emoji. Image-set items and an unknown id without a label stay plain ids.

Uploads made before Phase 5c whose ids (Math.random().toString(36).slice(2, 11)) are shorter than the 8 characters the device id rule needs, written as legacy-<id> device images (A42), with and without a label; a 9-character legacy id stays as it is.
